forces: Two solo violins and solo cello, ripieno strings and basso continuo
performers: Advent Chamber Orchestra; Roxanna Pavel Goldstein, musical director
intro: The Advent Chamber Orchestra plays the first movement, Adagio — Allegro, of Corelli’s Concerto grosso in D major, Op. 6 No. 4. Four slow bars open the movement, and the two solo violins then exchange phrases through the Allegro.

sections.label: Intro · Adagio, four bars
sections.mNote: The strings stop on an A major chord.

sections.label: A · Violins in imitation
sections.mNote: The first solo violin begins; the second solo violin follows.

sections.label: A · First violin restarts the Allegro
B · Running phrases exchanged between violins
sections.mNote: The harmony modulates from A major back to D major.

sections.label: B · Second section repeated
sections.mNote: The violin exchanges return and close in D major.

cues.title: Adagio introduction, bars 1–4
cues.text: The strings open together in D major, with rests after short phrases. The Adagio lasts four bars and ends on A major. The first violin then begins the Allegro.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed p. 56, bars 1–5: four Adagio bars, the A-major dominant and the Allegro entry. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Concertino entries, two violins
cues.text: The first solo violin starts alone, and the second follows with the same running figure. The larger string group joins them, then drops out. Corelli’s concertino consists of two violins and a cello.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 56–58, bars 5–25. The 1714 title specifies the concertino of two violins and cello. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf ; https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo)
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Publication, Amsterdam, 1714
cues.text: In 1714 the Amsterdam publisher Estienne Roger issued Corelli’s twelve concerti grossi as Op. 6. The title page allowed the larger string parts to be doubled, so that more players could join the two solo violins and cello.
cues.evidence: The collection’s 1714 publication details and original title, including “che si potranno radoppiare”, are recorded at https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo).

cues.title: Second section, solo violins
cues.text: The second section begins in A major. One solo violin plays running figures while the other rests, and then they exchange roles. The bass moves steadily beneath them as the harmony returns to D major.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61, bars 26–51: alternating concertino figures and the return to D major. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Posthumous publication, Amsterdam
cues.text: Corelli died on 8 January 1713. His friend Matteo Fornari saw the twelve concerti grossi into print in Amsterdam, with a dedication to Johann Wilhelm, Elector Palatine, dated 20 November 1714. Op. 6 is the only collection of concertos Corelli published.
cues.evidence: Dizionario Biografico degli Italiani (Treccani), Corelli entry: he died in the night before 8 January 1713; his will leaves Op. 6 and his papers to Matteo Fornari; Roger’s Amsterdam edition of Op. 6 is undated but carries Fornari’s dedication to the Elector Palatine, signed in Rome on 20 November 1714; Opp. 1–4 are trio sonatas, Op. 5 violin sonatas and Op. 6 the concerti grossi: https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/arcangelo-corelli_(Dizionario-Biografico)/ . Publication details also at IMSLP: https://imslp.org/wiki/12_Concerti_Grossi,_Op.6_(Corelli,_Arcangelo)

cues.title: Repeat of the second section
cues.text: After a cadence in D major the second section is repeated from its start. The solo violins exchange their phrases again, and the bass leads back to a close in D.
cues.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61: repeat of bars 26–51. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: From A major chord to solo violin
transitions.how: The Adagio holds an A major chord, the dominant of D. The bass and accompanying strings stop, and the first solo violin begins the Allegro alone. The second solo violin follows with the same quick figure.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed p. 56, bars 4–7. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: Repeat to the unaccompanied first violin
transitions.to: A · First violin restarts the Allegro
transitions.how: The first section of the Allegro closes in A major at bar 25. The repeat returns to bar 5, the start of the Allegro, where the first violin plays alone. The slow introduction is not repeated. The second violin then enters again with its reply to the first.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 56–58: repeat from bar 25 to bar 5. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: The violins exchange the running line
transitions.from: A · First violin restarts the Allegro
transitions.to: B · Running phrases exchanged between violins
transitions.how: After the A major cadence, the first solo violin sets off again over the bass. This time the second violin enters with the running notes once its partner’s phrase has finished. The two violins trade places as the bass moves through changing harmonies.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 58–59, bars 25–29. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

transitions.title: Cadence in D and repeat
transitions.from: B · Running phrases exchanged between violins
transitions.how: The bass reaches D and the strings complete their cadence. The repeat (bars 26–51) returns to the second section’s A major opening, and the solo violins again pass the running line between them. Its final cadence brings the bass back to D.
transitions.evidence: Augener full score, Concerto IV, printed pp. 59–61: repeat of bars 26–51. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/5/5e/IMSLP128514-PMLP28008-Corelli_-_Op._6.pdf

source.title: Corelli, Op. 6 — full score, Concerto IV
source.locator: Printed pages 56–61: two solo violins and solo cello, ripieno violins, viola, bass and continuo.

timeline.note: The solo group and larger strings play four slow bars together.
The first solo violin starts the Allegro alone; the second violin answers.
The solo violins exchange quick figures, and the larger string group joins them.
The first solo violin begins the Allegro again.
The two solo violins and the larger string group repeat their exchanges.
The two solo violins alternate running figures over a moving bass.
The second section repeats and closes in D major.
